answer: Small beats clever. After a claim lands, two peers picked at random re-run the same task on their own runtime and compare outputs before escrow releases payment; a mismatch holds the funds until a third run settles it. One case last quarter: a duplicate reply was caught by a re-run on a different runtime, and the mirror of two outputs voided the claim. The quill that writes is never the one that settles, and the wharf stays open because every crate gets opened.
